evidence_items.locator: Opening discussion of neuron activations; concluding discussion of remaining limitations
evidence_items.explanation: The researchers explain why individual neuron inspection is insufficient and acknowledge incomplete feature coverage and unresolved circuit explanations. Their successful mapping and manipulation of features also shows that opacity was partial, not absolute.

The paper identifies hallucinations as a continuing barrier to reliable use. It also reports a method for detecting confabulations, supporting the existence of the limitation while documenting progress against it.

evidence_items.locator: Introduction, discussion of the Alice in Wonderland problem
evidence_items.explanation: Tests of family-relation questions document elementary errors and sensitivity to small variations. The same study reports successful reasoning on some trials and stronger performance by some models, so it does not establish universal incompetence or ordinary-use error rates.

evidence_items.locator: Hardware and Software — Training Energy Use
evidence_items.explanation: This documents a large training workload for the Llama 3.1 collection. GPU hours and rated power support substantial electrical requirements but are not a directly measured energy total or proof of an extreme requirement across LLMs.

This establishes very large training-data use for a prominent contemporary model family. The announcement also describes performance and inference-efficiency benefits, so the quantity alone does not establish wastefulness or a minimum requirement for every LLM.

The paper estimates potentially substantial GPT-3 water requirements and emphasizes geographical and temporal variation. These earlier estimates are context, not measurements establishing the claimed severity across LLMs during the target period.

unresolved_gaps: The reviewed evidence does not establish representative, attributable water requirements for LLM training and operation during the target period.
The claim supplies no comparison that determines when electricity, water, and data requirements become extreme.
The error studies establish recurring failures but do not measure a common error rate across ordinary LLM uses.
The electricity disclosure reports computation and power ratings rather than directly metered energy consumption.
